notes.title: Devlog #1 - Introductions
notes.content:
Hey miners! 

Left Stranded is a game I am building solo as a spare time project but that I am fully committed to finish and release! Let me give some context first.

[b]Left Stranded so far[/b]

I started developing this game over 3 years ago, at the time I was using Unity, before all the drama with the Runtime Fee.. let’s not go there. At the time the game was already a 2d factory game, but it was following the sci-fi wagon, usual script Factorio style, a lone engineer/scientist left on a land, build things to save himself and somehow escape.  At some point along the line I lost interest in the project, mainly because I couldn’t find any traction/interest, mainly for bad marketing and bad social platform of choice (Twitter) to post updates. 

[b]A new beginning[/b]

Last year, once all the dust cleared out after the Unity debacle, a new shiny engine raised from ashes.. Godot.. at the time I didn’t really know the engine, not GDScript, so just out of curiosity, I started using it for very simple projects, following tutorials, reading documentation and I have been instantly hooked by how easy it was to add multiplayer support to a Godot game… so I thought… let’s rewrite Left Stranded from scratch and let’s redesign it to be a multiplayer game from the get-go.

I didn’t want to recreate the same game, so after some thinking and a lot of support from the Discord community which I am building around this game, I decided that Left Stranded is going to be a multiplayer factory automation game set in Medieval age! 

In a nutshell, the player will be blacksmith which has been cast away from his kingdom and the only way to claim back his life is to provide the kingdom with enough goods like armours, weapons, helms and shields to repay his debts. They will have to build complex and preforming factory system to pickup with the requests from the kingdom.

[b]Conveyor Belts[/b]

I started from the very basics, conveyor belts! 

Being set in a medieval age it made sense to have belts to be made of solid wood. I added an animation in place (it is actually a shader) which simulates the sliding effect of a single belt section to communicate to the player which direction that belt section is moving item to. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42181904/07b8a255220187d0ae456db2f908b69b8c604ecd.gif[/img]

[b]Resources[/b]

There is a total of 6 different ore types that the players can mine in the game:

Stone, Copper, Gold, Platinum and Selenium ores can be smelted to create ingots which can be used as ingredients in recipes to build machines, belts, goods. 

Coal is a special one which is going to be the main source of energy/fuel to power the machines.

Water is going to be crucial as well. I still have to wrap my head around it, but I want water to be either a way to power machines or a way to ship goods back to the Kingdom.

[b]Mining[/b]

For a factory automation game, mining is probably the most important feature of the game, I wanted the player to be able to mine both manually, with a cool a shiny pickaxe, and also by placing a Mine ‘machine’, which can be attached to a belt system to automate the process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42181904/7c70d024663618a4b58c2d1ba1b2adb6d2b94ac9.gif[/img]

The Mine machine once placed, scans the surrounding area (3x3) and looks for ore deposits within range. Once a belts system is connected to the output, the machine starts extracting ores from the surrounding deposits. I set the mining speed to be 1 ore each 5 seconds which works pretty well in terms of the speed new items get added to the belts.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42181904/463baee14d7d96932618ea5fb76314363620c836.gif[/img]

In the next post I will probably cover how I setup procedural terrain generation and multiplayer,  this one got quite long already, so it is time to wrap up.

Thanks a lot for reading thus far and I would love to get your feedback on my Discord server! 

Discord server link: [url=https://discord.gg/5eQynQRGUK]https://discord.gg/5eQynQRGUK[/url]

Andy

notes.title: Devlog #1 -Left Stranded
notes.content:
I decided to start this devlog to keep track of my progress on the game but also to keep you guys up to speed about whatever I have been working on. 

I will try to consistently post new devlogs every couple of weeks, I think it would be a good time frame to be able to present something compelling and hopefully interesting.

Since the game is in the middle of development, I am trying to cover as many aspects of the game as I can. But here it is a summary of this past two weeks:

[b]Graphics Updates[/b]

I am at the beginning of my experience with pixelart, but I believe I am getting better overtime. 
I started revamping all machines and rocks models moving from 16x16 to 32x32 textures.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42181904/e49987dde75ae8d5620cc769e18a99b5b9ff47d7.png[/img]

The new models define a more clear art style and give that simple and direct cool vibe to the game. Increasing the texture size to 32x32 was I big step for me but that additional space allowed me to put more content into a single model.

[b]Procedurally generated[/b]

When I started working on the game, I envisioned a very simple environment with a small map, hand crafted where I would have been able to add content to it as I pleased, manually. But then, I arrived to the realization that I was wasting a lot of precious time for something that could have been "easily" automated. 

I started working on making the entire world completely autogenerated using a set of well known generation strategies involving Perlin Noise, Cellular Automata and Poisson Disk Placement. Using these techniques, I came up with a map generator which can potentially create infinite types of maps (actually planets) for the player to explore!

Having procedurally generated maps should increase replyability of the game and hopefully make the players more engaged. I will show more details about how the generation works in another devlog probably, but this is how the rendering of a single chunk of the map from Unity looks like:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42181904/cee8edf7c3406e424e0b7d00bba0c0dd0e3e5684.png[/img]

That's it for this devlog, hope you guys liked what you saw! If you want to follow the process up close you can follow me on Twitter [url=https://twitter.com/dev_bre]@dev_bre[/url], and... please don't forget to wishlist! That is crucial for my game to be exposed on Steam and get traction!

Until next time!
Andy
